Before I touch anything, one thing about "clean things up": it can mean a dozen different things (dead code, untracked junk, formatting, deps, structure), and unrequested cleanup is exactly where unreviewed changes hide. So let me first take a **read-only** look at what's actually here, then come back to you with a concrete, scoped list — you pick what's in bounds and I'll keep the diff traced to that.

Running a survey, no writes:

TOOL: pwd && git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null; git status --short --branch 2>/dev/null
TOOL: ls -la
TOOL: git log --oneline -10 2>/dev/null
TOOL: find . -maxdepth 2 -not -path './.git/*' -not -path './node_modules/*' -not -path './.venv/*' -not -path './venv/*' | head -100
TOOL: ls -la; echo '--- untracked/ignored junk ---'; git status --ignored --short 2>/dev/null | head -50
TOOL: for f in .editorconfig .gitignore README.md README.rst pyproject.toml package.json Cargo.toml go.mod Makefile; do [ -e "$f" ] && echo "== $f =="; done

Give me the output and I'll turn it into a findings list (dead code, stray files, config drift, etc.), flag anything I'd *notice but not silently fix*, and ask you which buckets are in scope before making a single edit.
